newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Uzbek firm plans to build $225 mln alumina plant.
newsitem.headline: Uzbek firm plans to build $225 mln alumina plant.

text.p: Uzbek coal company Ugol plans to begin construction of a 200,000-tonne annual capacity alumina plant in the second half of 1997 in the Tashkent area, Interfax news agency on Thursday quoted the firm's director as saying.

Ugol general director Anatoly Leleko said a new company would be set up and offer shares in the $225 million plant, which would take about four years to build and use 1.5 million tonnes of kaolin, which Ugol produces incidentally each year.
He said shares would be offered to the Tursunzade aluminium smelter in Tajikistan and the Bratsk aluminium smelter in Russia.
Neither company was immediately available for comment.

The All-Russian Aluminium and Magnesium Institute of St Petersburg had made a feasibility study of the project and the Uzbek government had approved the design of the plant, to be built near the Angren coal field, Interfax quoted Leleko as saying.
The study reported that the Ugol venture could produce alumina at a cost 20-30 percent lower than Russian competitors, he said, but he did not give absolute figures.
